decisions.reason: As a close-to-core earmold product in a growing innovative med-tech business, management would likely keep it, but its limited visibility over time suggests results may be below aspiration and raises discontinuation risk.
This custom in-ear earmold fits the firm's established hearing-systems activities and was launched prominently, so with no clear sign of shortfall it would likely remain on the market.
The thermoforming unit supports the firm's integrated workflow offering and uses existing technical capabilities, making retention more likely unless performance clearly misses aspiration levels.

Although this orthopedic shoe last is distant from the core business and therefore faces a higher review threshold, it is still a recent launch and organisational slack makes one more year of trial plausible.

The post-curing unit is close to the firm's digital production and materials business, so it is likely to be retained while market feedback accumulates, though its modest prominence leaves moderate uncertainty.
